title: Google Analytics vs Plausible
description: Compare Google Analytics 4 and Plausible Analytics on privacy, pricing, performance, and ease of use for websites of all sizes.
verdict: Choose Plausible if you need cookieless, GDPR-friendly analytics with a lightweight script. Choose GA4 if you need deep integration with Google Ads, BigQuery, and enterprise-scale reporting at no direct cost.
quickAnswer: **Plausible** is the better fit if privacy compliance, simplicity, and page-speed matter more than deep ad-platform integration. **Google Analytics 4** is the better fit if you rely on Google's advertising ecosystem, need BigQuery export, or want a free, full-featured analytics suite.
bottomLine: There is no universal winner. Plausible wins on privacy, simplicity, and speed. GA4 wins on ecosystem integration and cost (for most sites). Many teams migrating away from Universal Analytics choose Plausible; teams running paid search often stay on GA4.

faq.question: Is Plausible GDPR compliant without a cookie banner?
faq.answer: Plausible is designed to work without cookies and without collecting personal data, which often eliminates the need for a cookie consent banner in many EU jurisdictions. Always verify with your legal counsel for your specific use case.

faq.question: Is Google Analytics 4 free?
faq.answer: GA4 is free for the vast majority of websites. Google Analytics 360 is the paid enterprise tier for organizations with very high data volumes or advanced support needs.

faq.question: Which has a smaller script size?
faq.answer: Plausible uses a significantly smaller tracking script than GA4's gtag.js bundle. See our benchmarks page for recorded measurements once published.

faq.question: Can I use both GA4 and Plausible together?
faq.answer: Yes. Some teams run Plausible as a privacy-friendly primary dashboard while keeping GA4 for ad attribution. This adds script weight and complexity, so weigh the tradeoff carefully.

editorialNotes.title: Performance
editorialNotes.content: Plausible's script is designed to be lightweight. GA4's gtag.js loads additional Google libraries that can increase main-thread work. We publish recorded benchmark data on our [benchmarks hub](/benchmarks/) — never estimated numbers.
